governance.parent: Facultad de Artes, Universidad de Chile

basis: The mission page says the museum depends on the Facultad de Artes of the Universidad de Chile.
The 2024 annual report, chapter 1 (PDF page 4), says the museum was formed by and depends on a private-law foundation whose board draws on human rights organisations and universities.
The foundation page gives the private-law nonprofit form and the five-member board, and the transparency page says the foundation publishes its information under Law 20.285.

Law 21.045 (version of 29 September 2025), article 29 makes the museum an integral part of the Servicio Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural and article 38 binds the Service's staff to the Estatuto Administrativo.

governance.parent: Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee

basis: The March 2026 recruitment notice lists the museum among 17 units directly under the Publicity Department and says units other than two named companies are public institutions on the state public-institution pay system.

governance.parent: Publicity Department of the Beijing Municipal Committee of the Communist Party of China

basis: The 2025 budget statement, part 1 section I, calls the museum a public-interest class 1 public institution under the Beijing Municipal Party Committee's Publicity Department with 147 establishment posts and no administrative posts.
The Ministry of Culture and Tourism's page lists the museum among its directly affiliated units.
